flags.reasoning: 'an ally from the same squad' has no squad axis in the data, so it is expressed as a slug list (same precedent as noir's burst same-squad gate). I am BLIND to data/characters.json here and cannot verify Anchor's squad roster; the list is a recollection-level guess. A wrong list makes the block inert (under-credit) rather than over-firing, which is the safe direction because the heal drives teammates' on-recovery triggers.
flags.recipe: Read the squad/lore field for anchor-innocent-maid (and each candidate) in data/characters.json or the blablalink profile; replace the slugs array with the confirmed same-squad roster, including the base anchor slug if it qualifies. Then confirm with a runComp trace that the heal's buffApply/recovery events appear only on rosters containing a listed ally.

flags.reasoning: 'Potency of HP ▲' is not a StatKey. Two readings: (a) Max HP ▲ (targetMaxHpPct), (b) a healing-potency / recovery-amount multiplier, which the schema cannot express at all. Reading (a) is literal-word-closest and is inert for damage (ally-granted Max HP does not feed a teammate's atkOfMaxHpPct, and this unit carries no HP→ATK scaler), so the choice moves no damage today. The step is retained regardless because escalating indexes by position — dropping it would promote the Distributed Damage step to the FIRST Full Burst, a real over-credit.
flags.recipe: Confirm the stat's in-game display name on the blablalink kit page / the datamined stat id. If it is a recovery-amount stat, move the line verbatim to unmodeled.skill1 and replace the step with the nearest inert placeholder that preserves the index, or add a healing-potency StatKey if a consumer ever exists. Either way re-check that the Distributed Damage buff first appears on the SECOND full burst in a runComp buffApply trace.

flags.estimate: 10.13 Hit Rate → engine hrCoreMult core-hit lift (magnitude of the lift itself unmeasured)
flags.reasoning: The 10.13% is verbatim from the kit, but the Hit-Rate→core-rate conversion is a derived engine relationship (sim.ts hrCoreMult, HRCORE-gated), not a measured per-unit constant. The damage this line produces is therefore only as good as that global slope, and it is an ALWAYS-⚑ field by policy.
flags.recipe: Do not tune the 10.13 (kit-true). Validate the downstream lift on a recorded fight: run the control comp with HRCORE=1 vs HRCORE=0 in SEPARATE processes (module-const env flag), compare the focus unit's core-hit fraction delta against the accuracy-circle geometry in docs/data/sg-calc/ / HRCORE, and refine the slope there, not here.

flags.field: base cadence tuple (RL: chargeFrames 60, reloadFrames 141, ammo 6) — consumer of skill2 reloadSpeedPct 40.04
flags.estimate: use the datamined tuple as-is; reload buff payoff ≈ 141f/1.4004 ≈ 101f per cycle on a 6-round RL
flags.reasoning: rate_of_fire / reloadFrames are known-unreliable datamine fields, and the effective cadence is frame-quantised (60fps boundaries). The reload-speed step's entire value is mediated by the reload frame count and the charge time, so a wrong tuple silently mis-prices a modeled damage line.
flags.recipe: Read the reload cycle + charge time off a recording of this unit (ammo-counter timestamps between empty and refill, and trigger-pull to shot-landing for the charge), quantise to 60fps frame boundaries, and correct the character entry before grading this override's reload contribution.

flags.estimate: burstCast for the burst block; escalating counters monotonic, never reset
flags.reasoning: Trigger identity is read literally — the burst block is her own cast (fires only on rotations where she actually bursts, and lands pre-FB so it takes no +50% major, correct for a buff), while skill1/skill2 are team-wide FB enter/end and fire on ANY chain. The kit is SILENT on whether the 'number of times used' counters reset (per battle vs per something else); I assume monotonic per battle, which is the standard escalating semantic.
flags.recipe: In a recorded multi-rotation fight, check that the Distributed Damage / Reload Speed tiers persist from the 2nd/3rd Full Burst onward and never revert to tier 1; if they revert, the counter resets and the escalating primitive needs a reset rule (a per-rotation everyN/offset shape) instead.
